description: Sell, exchange, give away certificate of title or identification number plate.
decision: Two third-degree felonies cover knowingly dealing in a salvage title or plate sold contrary to the section, and dealing in a detached original plate. The required-repair exception remains applicable.

description: Manufacture, exchange, or possess vessel with counterfeit or wrong ID number.
decision: One branch covers counterfeit or wrongly assigned vessel identification plates, with an approved replacement exception. The other covers knowing dealings in a vessel or part with an altered number, or concealment of its identity. Paragraph (c) grades both as third-degree felonies.

description: Transmission of material harmful to minors to a minor by electronic device or equipment.
decision: Both third-degree choices require a knowing or believed transmission of material harmful to minors to a specific recipient known or believed to be a minor. Subsection (3) specifies a sender outside Florida. Subscription-based transmissions are excluded.

description: Aggravated assault; intent to commit felony.
decision: The retained aggravated assault choice includes assault with intent to commit a felony as an alternative to the deadly-weapon branch. The ordinary grade is a third-degree felony; the underlying assault elements still apply.

description: Distributing, offering to distribute, or possessing with intent to distribute obscene materials depicting minors.
decision: The child-depiction branch grades the specified knowing distribution, offer or possession with intent of obscene material depicting a minor engaged in an act harmful to minors as a third-degree felony. The chart description does not establish every offense in the section.

description: Practicing medical physics without a license.
decision: Practicing or attempting medical physics, or holding oneself out as licensed without an active license, is a third-degree felony, subject to the statutory exemptions. The sampled act does not depend on the false-statement or misuse-of-license branches.

description: Committing vehicular homicide and failing to render aid or give information.
decision: The broader vehicular homicide choice includes the first-degree branch for a reckless killing when the driver knew or should have known of the crash and failed the information and aid duties. Knowledge of injury or death is unnecessary.

description: Trafficking in amphetamine, 28 grams or more, less than 200 grams.
decision: The first-degree amphetamine trafficking choice expressly identifies 28 to less than 200 grams, seven years mandatory minimum and a $100,000 fine. It belongs to the separately gated 101-record family.

description: Sexual battery; engage in sexual conduct with minor 12 to 18 years by person in familial or custodial authority.
decision: Prior choices required other age, force or consent circumstances. This first-degree felony punishable up to life instead requires familial or custodial authority over a victim aged 12 through 17 and sexual battery, regardless of willingness.

description: Trafficking in phencyclidine, 400 grams or more.
decision: The first-degree phencyclidine trafficking choice includes 400 grams or more, a 15-year mandatory minimum and a $250,000 fine. It belongs to the separately gated 101-record family.

description: Kidnapping; child under age 13, perpetrator also commits aggravated child abuse, sexual battery, or lewd or lascivious battery, molestation, conduct, or exhibition.
decision: Ordinary kidnapping did not capture the life felony. The new choice covers a child under 13 and aggravated child abuse, sexual battery against the child or a listed lewd act during kidnapping. It claims only subparagraphs 1 through 3, the predicates in the sampled description.
